data.narrative:
Core Automation, a stealth-stage AI & Software company founded by Gerald Depew and Daniel C. Rozok, is currently targeting a Series funding round of $500M–$1B at a post-money valuation of $4–5B+. The relevant comparison universe comprises nine private peers (including Palantir, Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition) and one public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR), representing the broader frontier AI & Software sector.

Peer-median valuation analysis proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables. The dataset identified twelve same-sector peers in AI & Software, but zero companies matched the combined filters of stealth-stage equivalence, adjacent-stage proximity, and similar valuation tier. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of funding dynamics, technology maturity, and commercial traction across earlier and later stages. This methodological constraint significantly limits triangulation power.

The target-stated range of $4–5B+ reflects founder expectations and incoming investor pricing signals, but without sufficient narrow-peer multiples or comparable transaction data points, independent validation through standard VC methods cannot be completed. Key uncertainties include Core Automation's current revenue or customer traction (not disclosed), product differentiation relative to the named peer set, and burn rate relative to the $500M–$1B capital target. Further diligence on these operational metrics would be required to stress-test the stated valuation against sector precedent.
